repo_contract.delivery_path: branch -> pull request -> CI checks -> reviewed merge -> deploy

product.name: Lama Dev School Management Dashboard
product.primary_problem: Provide role-appropriate school operations, schedule, attendance, result, event, and announcement workflows from one dashboard.
critical_user_journeys: Administrator manages school structure and people records.
Teacher manages lessons, assignments, exams, attendance, and results.
Student views class schedule, assignments, exams, results, and attendance.
Parent views child-specific schedule, announcements, events, attendance, and results.

architecture.summary: Next.js App Router dashboard with Clerk-authenticated role surfaces, Prisma as the data access layer, and PostgreSQL as the system of record.
runtime_topology: Next.js application server renders role-specific dashboard routes and serves the dependency-light /health endpoint.
Clerk provides authentication and role metadata used by middleware and server components.
Prisma Client mediates application access to PostgreSQL.
Container builds generate Prisma Client and the Next.js production build without running database migrations.

critical_boundaries.auth: Role and identity decisions stay in Clerk middleware, Clerk helpers, and role-aware server components.
critical_boundaries.data: School records are persisted through Prisma models backed by PostgreSQL; avoid ad hoc database access paths.
critical_boundaries.deployment: Image build, migration deploy, app start, and health smoke are separate release steps.
critical_boundaries.secrets: Secrets come from process environment or the deployment platform and must not be committed.

release_risk_surfaces: Clerk auth, middleware matchers, and role routing.
Prisma schema, migrations, seed data, and database connection settings.
Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, CI workflow, and deployment environment variables.
Dashboard pages that expose student, parent, teacher, or administrator data.
architecture.decision_policy: Prefer small, reversible changes that preserve role-specific dashboard behavior. Require explicit design notes, verification evidence, and rollback notes for auth, Prisma, middleware, Docker, CI, or deployment changes.

reliability.service_level_intent: Protect role-specific dashboard availability, data correctness, and cross-role data separation before expanding product scope.

health_model.process_health: /health returns status ok without requiring Clerk, Prisma, or PostgreSQL so release automation can distinguish app-process health from dependency health.
health_model.dependency_health: Prisma, PostgreSQL, and Clerk health are verified through migration gates, release checks, authenticated journey smoke, and provider/runtime logs rather than the process health route.
health_model.post_deploy_smoke: Run npm run smoke:health against /health, then verify the highest-risk authenticated dashboard journey available in the target environment.

slo_candidates: /health process check success: 99.9% monthly after production launch.
Authenticated dashboard page availability: 99.5% monthly after production launch.
Critical dashboard server response target: p95 under 1000 ms after warm start.
Cross-role data visibility incidents: zero known incidents.
failure_modes: Clerk outage, missing session, or invalid role metadata blocks authenticated dashboard access.
PostgreSQL connection, migration, or Prisma Client failure blocks Prisma-backed pages.
Role routing regression exposes or hides records across admin, teacher, student, and parent surfaces.
Build-time or runtime environment gaps break production builds, starts, or authenticated views.
Docker or service-manager restart changes remap ports or report stale health evidence.

required_signals: Clerk authentication and authorization failure signals where available
blocked_signals: Production dashboards and alerting targets are not available in this workspace.
Browser end-to-end journey telemetry is not implemented.
Production traffic profile and capacity baseline are not available in this workspace.

operational_response.abort: Stop promotion when CI, migration, build, health smoke, critical audit, or role-access verification fails.
operational_response.rollback: Use previous_release runtime rollback or PR revert; Prisma changes require a backward-compatible migration plan and tested restore path before destructive schema work.

capacity_assumptions: The Next.js app is stateless aside from Clerk and PostgreSQL dependencies.
No production traffic or concurrency profile is available in this workspace.
Container healthchecks probe only dependency-light process health.
Scale and performance claims require target-environment metrics before release promotion.

owns: Next.js school management dashboard application code.
Repo-local release-readiness guidance, verification contract, and CI gates.
Application-level /health process check and smoke script.
does_not_own: Clerk provider availability or account configuration outside this repository.
Production PostgreSQL hosting, backups, or restore execution outside this workspace.
cynik service-manager credentials, target metadata, or production promotion approval.

operational_expectations: Release manager confirms CI evidence, rollback target, and required environment variables before promotion.
Engineering owner reviews auth, Prisma, middleware, Docker, CI, and deployment boundary changes before merge.
Incident commander coordinates rollback, customer-impact assessment, and follow-up notes for production incidents.
escalation_path: Start with the release manager for failed release gates or unclear promotion evidence.
Escalate to the engineering owner for code, data, auth, or migration defects.
Escalate to the incident commander for production-impacting outages, cross-role data exposure, or rollback decisions.
handoff_requirements: Name exact commands run and outcomes.
Name blocked gates and residual risk.
Confirm rollback path as PR revert or previous_release redeploy.
Record whether real deployment credentials, service manager, and target metadata were available.
open_owner_gaps: Named human owners are still TBD in owners.* and must be resolved before production promotion.
Production alert destinations, dashboard links, and service-manager runbooks are not available in this workspace.

release_promotion_checks: npx prisma migrate deploy against a disposable or controlled target database
deploy_facing_checks: docker build with required public build args
start the built app or image
restart validation where the deployment runtime supports it
regression_risk_controls: tests/contracts.test.mjs asserts governance, CI, Docker, and release-readiness contracts
tests/product-behavior.test.mjs guards role routing and high-value dashboard behavior
browser end-to-end coverage is still required before high-confidence authenticated-flow promotion
verification.evidence_policy: Record exact commands, outcomes, blockers, and residual risk in .codex/reports/release-readiness.md before handoff.
verification.blocked_gate_policy: Do not claim completion for a blocked gate. Name the blocker, affected release risk, and next safe step.

runtime_notes.local_node_observation: Local shell may differ from CI; Node 20 remains the contracted release verification runtime.

release.default_path: branch -> pull request -> CI checks -> reviewed merge -> deploy
release.strategy: Advisory-first hardening on a branch, followed by maintainer PR review and release-owner promotion after evidence review.
release.rollback_action: Redeploy previous_release or revert the pull request; do not run destructive database rollback without a tested restore plan.

risk_classification.current_hardening: configuration, documentation, contract tests, and release evidence only

promotion_gates: npx prisma migrate deploy against a disposable or controlled target database
start built app and run npm run smoke:health
deploy_sequence: Confirm target environment variables and previous release artifact.
Build the application or container image without database side effects.
Run Prisma migrations with npx prisma migrate deploy as an explicit release step.
Start or roll the app process.
Verify the highest-risk authenticated journey available in the target environment.
abort_conditions: Any required CI, verification, build, migration, or health-smoke gate fails.
Critical production dependency audit reports a vulnerability.
Production secrets, target metadata, rollback artifact, or deployment owner cannot be confirmed.
Role-based dashboard access cannot be verified for the release scope.

rollback.code: Revert the pull request or redeploy the previous known-good artifact.
rollback.database: Use backward-compatible Prisma migrations; after a committed migration, prefer app rollback to a version compatible with the new schema unless a tested restore plan exists.

evidence_required: Exact commands and outcomes recorded in .codex/reports/release-readiness.md.
Blocked gates and residual risks called out before handoff.

agile.planning_cadence: Small, reviewable pull requests. Major feature work starts with PRFAQ/problem framing and critical user journey mapping before implementation.
agile.backlog_policy: Prioritize work that reduces release risk, protects role-based school workflows, or improves evidence for production decisions.
definition_of_ready: Target user, user problem, and success metric are named.
Primary critical user journey and failure-sensitive points are documented.
Affected routes, Prisma models, auth roles, deploy surfaces, and rollback path are identified.
Required verification commands are selected from verification_contract.json.
definition_of_done: Behavior changes are covered by focused tests or documented as intentionally unchanged.
npm run verify passes, or blockers and residual risk are recorded in .codex/reports/release-readiness.md.
Deploy-facing changes include /health smoke evidence and rollback notes.
PR description links the product brief or journey update when the change is feature-facing.

release_planning.default_path: branch -> pull request -> CI checks -> reviewed merge -> deploy
release_planning.deployment_policy: No production deploy from an AI session; release owner approves promotion after evidence review.
release_planning.rollback_policy: Prefer PR revert or previous_release redeploy. Schema changes must use backward-compatible expand/contract steps until restore is tested.

agile.retro_policy: Capture reusable release lessons in AGENTS.md, .codex rules, docs/operations, or the release-readiness report before closing major nodes.

continuous_improvement.maturity_goal: Advance from discovered toward self_improving through advisory-first, PR-first, evidence-backed changes that preserve current product behavior.
ratchet_loops: Quarantine dirty worktree state before unrelated growth by using a branch, pull request, or timestamped evidence bundle.
Convert repeated release blockers into contract tests, repo-local guidance, or runbook updates.
Update .codex/reports/release-readiness.md with exact verification outcomes, blocked gates, and residual risks after each hardening pass.
Keep product-facing work tied to PRFAQ/problem framing and critical user journey evidence before broad implementation.
scorecard_inputs: required profile sections present and covered by tests
verification_contract.json present and referenced by AGENTS.md and .codex config
CI, audit, Prisma, build, smoke, and rollback evidence recorded
known blockers classified as active, blocked by credentials, or follow-up work
learning_capture: Store reusable operating lessons in AGENTS.md, .codex/rules, docs/operations, or docs/product.
Store node-specific evidence in .codex/reports or .codex/evidence instead of mixing it into product code.
Prefer new contract-test assertions when a governance requirement has failed more than once.
continuous_improvement.recurring_blocker_policy: When a mission blocker repeats, classify it as active, stale, credential-blocked, or superseded before retrying, then add evidence or a guardrail that prevents the same blocker from being rediscovered as unresolved.
next_improvement_candidates: Add browser end-to-end coverage for authenticated dashboard journeys.
Resolve non-critical production dependency advisories through behavior-tested dependency upgrade work.
Fill named human owners, alert destinations, and cynik service-manager runbook links before production promotion.
Publish the hardening branch through a writable remote so PR checks and maintainer review can run.

deploy_contract.runtime_artifact: Next.js production build or container image after verification
deploy_contract.env_file_source: process environment supplied by deployment platform; committed .env files are forbidden

required_gates: python syntax gate when Python files exist
npx prisma migrate deploy against disposable database
health smoke against started production build

Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml are hardened as a local release evidence path, but Docker Compose is not confirmed as the production deployment interface.
Production secrets, service manager, target metadata, and deployment credentials are not available in this workspace.
